archetype.name: Dual-Threat (veteran bridge)
archetype.definition: A 12-year veteran backup who wins on quick, accurate throws to his left and the occasional designed run, keeping Washington's offense on schedule when Jayden Daniels can't go rather than carrying it.

report.headline: Efficient, turnover-free relief work, now on hold with an MCL sprain
report.take:
Mariota is what he has been for a decade: a mobile, accurate-enough passer who keeps the ball out of harm's way and adds value with his legs. His career rushing totals ranked inside the top ten at the position in five different seasons, and his CPOE has been positive in most of them, including +3.2 last year. In 2026 he has been the Commanders' insurance policy. He took 45% of snaps in relief at Dallas and every snap against Seattle, then started Week 4 against Indianapolis and lasted only 16% of the snaps. He is now listed Out with a knee MCL sprain and sits as QB2 behind Daniels.

The production in that window was better than a backup usually gives you: 0.21 EPA per dropback (12th of 43), no interceptions, no fumbles lost and a +3.9 CPOE. The engine is the short game. On 30 throws under 10 air yards he completed 76.7% at +8.9 over expected for 0.389 EPA a play, and throws to his left were almost automatic at 75%. The Seattle game was the real test: he was an 8.5-point underdog against what is now the No. 2 defense, pressured on 40% of dropbacks, and still threw three touchdowns in a 33-31 win.

The numbers flatter him in a few places. The 7.8% TD rate ranks 4th, but three of his four scores came on just four red-zone attempts, and that kind of finishing doesn't hold on volume. His two deep touchdowns came on a 2-of-8 deep line with negative EPA. Split by game state, the picture is stark. When Washington trailed by nine or more he posted 0.604 EPA a play. Within one score he was at -0.014, roughly league average, with 38% success. Third downs were a problem: 26.7% conversion facing an average 7.4 yards to go.

One trait does look different. He has historically taken too many sacks under pressure, with pressure-to-sack rates of 31-42% in past seasons. This year it is 14.3%, 6th best, despite being pressured at the second-highest rate among qualifiers. That is on 57 dropbacks, so it is more a hint than a reinvention. The overall read: a competent, low-variance bridge QB whose real value is protecting the ball for a team that can't afford short fields, given a defense ranked 24th in EPA.

strengths.title: Accurate, on-time short passing
strengths.body: Most of his work came on quick throws, and he was precise with them: 76.7% completions at nearly nine points over expected, producing strong EPA. That fits his career profile of positive CPOE in modest-aDOT offenses, so it is the most bankable part of his game.

strengths.title: Ball security under heavy pressure
strengths.body: He has zero interceptions and zero lost fumbles despite being pressured on nearly 39% of dropbacks. His pressure-to-sack rate is the striking change: 14.3% now versus 31% last year and worse before that. The clean turnover sheet is partly sample luck, but his INT counts have been moderate for years. The sack avoidance is worth watching rather than assuming.

strengths.title: Legs still a real threat
strengths.body: His two designed runs went for 22 yards a carry, including a 35-yard day in a 16%-snap cameo against Indianapolis. Rushing has been part of his value every season, with top-ten rushing ranks through most of his Titans and Falcons years. Scrambles, by contrast, have been unproductive.

concerns.title: Inflated TD rate on tiny sample
concerns.body: Three touchdowns on four red-zone attempts and two deep scores on a 25% deep completion rate are carrying a top-five TD rate. Neither will hold on normal volume. His career TD totals have mostly sat in the middle of the pack.

concerns.title: Ordinary in competitive game states
concerns.body: When the game was within one score his efficiency was roughly average. A big share of his EPA came while trailing by nine or more, against softer coverage. Third downs have been the sticking point: he converted barely a quarter of them, with long distances to go adding to the difficulty.

concerns.title: Knee sprain and pressure exposure
concerns.body: He is Out with an MCL sprain and sits behind a healthy Daniels, so his near-term role is zero. When he does play, the line has let him be pressured at a rate ranking 35th of 36, and his bad-throw rate ranks 25th. That combination is a risky mix for a 33-year-old coming off a knee injury.

trend.note: Three games with snap shares of 45%, 100% and 16% make a path, not a trend. The full Seattle game (19/31, 183 yards, 3 TDs) is the best read of him, and the injury cut his Week 4 start short.

nextGame.headline: Out at San Francisco; matchup would be hard anyway
nextGame.body:
Mariota is ruled out for the Monday night trip to San Francisco, and Daniels started Week 5, so this one is about Daniels. If Mariota were somehow pressed into action, the profile is unkind. The 49ers allow the fewest explosive passes in the league and rank 6th against deep throws. That matches his own deep game, which was the weakest part of his season. The opening is underneath: San Francisco ranks 21st on short-pass EPA, which is exactly where he lives.

Availability cuts both ways. Washington is without Stefon Diggs (60% snap share), its second-most-targeted receiver. San Francisco is missing safety Marques Sigle, is without Dre Greenlaw to a suspension, and has Nick Bosa officially out, though Shanahan says Bosa has a chance. The bigger issue is game script: the 49ers' offense ranks 1st in pass EPA, and Washington is a 7.5-point underdog.

keyMatchups.title: No explosives allowed over the top
keyMatchups.body: San Francisco rarely gives up big pass plays and holds up on deep throws. That shuts down the low-percentage shot game that produced his two deep touchdowns. Whoever plays QB has to live on volume underneath.

keyMatchups.title: Short-area softness to attack
keyMatchups.body: The 49ers are below average defending short throws. The absence of Greenlaw and Sigle in the second level and back end should widen those windows. This is the only real lever for a Washington passer.

keyMatchups.title: Chasing the top passing offense
keyMatchups.body: Washington's pass defense ranks 25th, and San Francisco's passing offense ranks 1st. Trailing script is likely, which inflates attempts but has historically flattered his garbage-time numbers more than his one-score play.

nextGame.watch: Whether he practices at all this week. Any return to practice signals how soon he is back as Daniels' insurance, and nothing more.

restOfSeason.body:
As QB2 behind a healthy Daniels, Mariota's rest-of-season value is contingency. If the knee heals on the estimated timeline and he is needed again, expect the version he has always been. That means efficient short passing, low interception risk and a few meaningful runs, inside a run-leaning offense that passes 3.2 points below expectation. His touchdown rate and red-zone finishing will come down hard toward his career norms. The sack avoidance under pressure is the trait to watch: if it holds, he is a better emergency starter than his 2025 tape suggested.

The ranges below are per start, not per week, since most weeks he won't play.
